newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 87 -2 on last week
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 140 -3 on last week
Cattle yardings in NSW this week were down four percent to 16,658 head. Cattle slaughter in the week fell 10 percent to 37,308 head.
In Queensland, cow, bullock and young cattle prices are broadly in line with September although well below October. In Victoria, prices are 10-20 cents a kg lower.

In the last South Korean tender awarded late last Friday, for 9,458 tonnes, Australian exporters won a surprisingly large 86 percent of the 4,200 tonnes of grassfed quarter beef on offer. Average prices, however, were down by 14 cents to 175 cents a kg compared with the last tender. Prices for position
After a wet winter and early spring in recent weeks, negligible rain has been received over much of western Victoria. This and concern about future prices is causing cattle to be turned off.

In Australia's north, however, cattle supplies remain reasonably low. In Queensland, yardings this week totalled 15,094 head, down nine percent. Total adult slaughter in Queensland in the week rose six percent to 48,186 head, eight percent below the equivalent week in 1995.

Australia won the rights to supply all the grassfed fullsets on offer, 828 tonnes. Prices were down by 32 cents a kg on the previous tender. Australian exporters also won all 600 tonnes of the grainfed quarter beef on offer.
In the U.S. this week, prices for Australian manufacturing beef were lower by about 5-8 cents a kg. The market appeared to strengthen slightly toward the end of the week.

There is still a severe shortage in the U.S. of grade choice cattle. Total cattle slaughter in the U.S. for the seven days to November 14 was 669,000 head, down 10,000 head from the previous week and up 9,680 head on a year ago.

In Japan, export prices for grassfed product, particularly loin cuts, fell sharply this week. Grassfed striploins fell by 48 cents a kg, or seven percent. Chilled grassfed fullsets were 12 cents a kg lower to average 34 cents a kg.
Additional supplies are now reaching Japan but demand remains subdued. On tight supplies in mid-October, wholesale prices rose for chilled grassfed cube rolls, striploins, tenderloins and fullsets.
Supplies of beef to Japan remain well below last year. October imports are estimated at 42,000 tonnes and November imports at 44,000 tonnes, about 25 percent less than last year.
